_note: Twenty-five sums. The FREE SEVEN are chosen by measurement, not by taste: between them they reach every claim the tool's header makes, so no part of the argument sits behind the paywall. 1 (48-23) needs NO exchange at all - the first rung of the didactic sequence, and the only record that lets the tool ask whether there is enough there; without it that hint was a genuinely dead string, which the locale smoke digest found and no assertion did. 2 and 3 are one borrow, twice, so it reads as a method rather than a trick. 4 puts a zero in the ones and still needs no cascade. 5 is the payload - the tens are empty, so the hundreds must be broken first, which is Brown & VanLehn's reliable impasse and the highest-information problem in the domain. 6 and 7 run the same latch the other way: one carry, then a cascading one. THE BORROW IS FREE ON PURPOSE - paywalling it would leave a free tier that demonstrates addition, and addition is not the topic teachers dread. The paid eighteen are depth: more of every shape, wider three-digit spreads, and the across-zero family that four separate documented bugs all fire on.
